newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ATHLETICS-EUROPEAN CHAMPION NEGURA BANNED FOR STEROID USE.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-EUROPEAN CHAMPION NEGURA BANNED FOR STEROID USE.

text.p: Romanian Iulia Negura has been banned for two years and stripped of her 1996 European women's cross-country championship title for failing a dope test, the Romanian Athletic Federation said on Wednesday.
"The Romanian Athletic Federation has banned Iulia Negura from all national and international competitions for a two-year period, dating from December 4, 1996," the Federation said in a statement.
Negura, 30, tested positive for the anabolic steroid stanozolol after winning the gold medal at the 1996 European cross-country championships in the Belgian town of Charleroi.
The Romanian national team also lose the silver medal they won for finishing in second place.

Both Negura and her coach Dorin Melinte denied she had taken a banned substance and Melinte quit his job as national long distance athletics coach after the announcement, saying he could no longer work in an "atmosphere of suspicion".
"Both Iulia Negura and her trainer Dorin Melinte say she took no banned substances," the Federation statement said.
"If such substances were found in samples, this could be due to a malicious act for which, unfortunately, they have no evidence for the moment."
The ruling was announced after a second urine sample, tested in Cologne, Germany, confirmed the initial positive result.
Several instances of doping have tarnished the image of Romanian athletics as competitors have sought the big cash prizes and foreign contracts to escape post-Communist poverty.
Nine athletes, eight of them women, have been banned in the last three years. Among them was 1993 indoor world champion long jumper Marieta Ilcu -- banned two years later.

Federation president Iolanda Balas told Reuters officials had limited Negura's ban to two years, instead of four years as stipulated by the International Athletics Federation, as the offence was her first in a long career.
"A two-year ban is in accordance with a directive from the Romanian sports ministry introduced last year and applicable to all doping cases in all sports," she said.
"In Iulia Negura's defence was the fact that she had been tested on repeated occasions with no violations."
